title: Odd-register branch semantics
statement: Let a nondeterministic register program with oracle, input, and guard be fixed. Suppose its instruction at state $l$ tests whether register $r$ is odd, the guard holds at the configuration with state $l$, register values $v$, and no answer recorded, and the corresponding odd branch at state $l_1$ has terminating semantics with acceptance equivalent to a proposition $P$. If $v(r)$ is odd, then the configuration at state $l$ has terminating semantics with acceptance equivalent to $P$.
hypotheses_covered: instruction at $l$ is the oddness test on $r$ with branches $l_1,l_0$
odd successor configuration has the stated terminating semantics for $P$
